subjects.introduction: Every Messenger of God, Bahá’u’lláh teaches, has been met with denial, derision and violence, most often at the hands of the very leaders who held the keys to recognition, and frequently by people who had long prayed for His coming. That pattern sets a question before anyone who meets hostility for their beliefs: how to tell honest disagreement from slander, and slander from persecution, without treating every critic as an enemy. The Báb struck in a governor’s hall, a nine-year-old hiding from stones in Tehran, a family carried out of a city in baggage carts: these are faces, not statistics, and they ask what care the vulnerable deserve from those who are safe. The counsel that answers them refuses revenge, prays for the calumniator, guards the tongue, and still petitions rulers for inquiry and justice, a stance that invites comparison with the Sermon on the Mount’s love of enemies. From here the path leads into the heedlessness that veils hearts, the steadfastness that endures without hardening, and the grief and martyrdom through which a persecuted community discovers its own strength.

order.why: Begin by distinguishing those who have not heard a teaching, those who question or reject it, and those who inflict harm. The readings ask how inherited expectations, imitation, and attachment to a particular interpretation can obstruct recognition. The complete narratives in the Kitáb-i-Íqán preserve the reasoning behind the examples rather than isolating accusations of unbelief. Other passages distinguish a teaching from the misconduct of its adherents and value understanding over mere imitation. The actual neighbors on heedlessness and on the rejection of Christ extend this enquiry. What evidence would enable a person to reconsider a judgment? How might a community resist persecution without treating every disagreement as persecution?
shortened: Consider the past. How many, both high and low, have, at all times, yearningly awaited the advent of the Manifestations of God in the sanctified persons of His chosen Ones. How often have they expected His coming, how frequently have they prayed that the breeze of divine mercy might blow, and the promised Beauty step forth from behind the veil of concealment, and be made manifest to all the world. And whensoever the portals of grace did open, and the clouds of divine bounty did rain upon mankind, and the light of the Unseen did shine above the horizon of celestial might, they all denied Him, and turned away from His face -- the face of God Himself.

Shouldst thou acquaint thyself with the indignities heaped upon the Prophets of God, and apprehend the true causes of the objections voiced by their oppressors, thou wilt surely appreciate the significance of their position. Moreover, the more closely thou observest the denials of those who have opposed the Manifestations of the divine attributes, the firmer will be thy faith in the Cause of God.

The criticism of religious leaders is accompanied by explicit praise of learned people who act justly. Preserve that distinction when reading the sharp polemical language. Accounts of commissions, coerced witnesses, altered writings and disputed histories raise questions about how claims are established. These remain the assertions and perspectives of their particular sources; a reported conversation or a summary written from memory is not an authenticated transcript. One letter acknowledges contradictory reports, and another asks that criticism of a Sultan be removed because he is no longer persecuting. The isolated report BHU0053 lacks the antecedent of its reference to contents; its context must not be invented. Explore the actual neighbors on Ottoman investigations and Covenant-breaking. What would fair inquiry require when an accuser also supplies the witnesses? How can a response correct misinformation without reproducing it?
shortened: O concourse of divines! When My verses were sent down, and My clear tokens were revealed, We found you behind the veils. This, verily, is a strange thing. Ye glory in My Name, yet ye recognized Me not at the time your Lord, the All-Merciful, appeared amongst you with proof and testimony. We have rent the veils asunder. Beware lest ye shut out the people by yet another veil. Pluck asunder the chains of vain imaginings, in the name of the Lord of all men, and be not of the deceitful.

The supplied wording differs in spelling and punctuation from the exact local record, so its approximate catalogue status and wording remain. How does the invitation to examine a claim for oneself shape the response to slander?

This extract from A Traveller’s Narrative reports an accusation made to the governor. The following passage says the search found only the Báb, His uncle and one companion, before His release on condition of leaving the city. Read that continuation at the primary source. The supplied an’ and mediates are retained rather than silently corrected to an and meditates. What is the difference between preserving an accusation as historical evidence and accepting its truth?

This authorized passage from A Traveller’s Narrative records the public mistreatment of three named missionaries. Read it with the surrounding account of the Báb’s return and the subsequent investigation; it remains an approximate imported reference rather than a verified corpus alignment. How does retaining names and the sequence of events change a reader’s attention to persecution?

The published Promulgation of Universal Peace talk places the exile narrative beside an explanation of selflessness, service, peace and the development of human capacities. Read the complete talk at the linked source. The local ABU0223 passage is a different provisional rendering and has not been substituted. What purpose does the speaker give to the endurance described here?

God Passes By places this authorized translated prayer within the account of the winter journey from Persia. Its surrounding words describe deprivation of food and water and the exposure of frail travelers and young children. The quoted prayer is itself excerpted in that publication; neither its gaps nor the supplied final omission have been invented away. The differently worded provisional local record has not been substituted. How does the physical setting shape this prayer?

The underlying authorized paragraph concerns a concealed gathering place for worship, even beneath the ground, in circumstances of hostility. Its final wording differs from this supplied rendering; the verified portion is retained without authorizing the variant ending. Read the complete paragraph in the compilation on the Mashriqu’l-Adhkár. What do the surrounding words reveal about the purpose of concealment?

God Passes By locates this translated warning within the early Baghdad period and describes the internal dissensions around it. The exact local BH04415 paragraph uses a different provisional translation. Preserve the supplied translation and approximate status, and consult the primary account for the surrounding counsel. What changes when a warning is read in its historical setting?

Crisis and Victory identifies this portion of the Tablet as translated by Shoghi Effendi and follows it with the example of Mary Magdalene encouraging the disciples. The local AB00348 version differs and has not been substituted. Read the complete published extract. How does an example of one person’s constancy contribute to the passage’s account of collective strength?

The letter of 24 June 1936 was written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi. Its continuation calls for wisdom, moderation and abstention from provocation; read it with the supplied paragraph. The supplied blessing and compared differ from the published blessings and compares and remain unchanged. How does that practical qualification affect the interpretation of trials as a source of growth?

Under Divine Destiny and Human Frailty, Bahá’í Administration follows this question with a call to inward examination, united effort and the discharge of responsibilities. It expressly resists attributing every setback to divine decree. The exact supplied wording is retained as an unmatched import. How can confidence in a spiritual purpose sharpen responsibility for avoidable mistakes?

The Advent of Divine Justice identifies the means of the preceding twofold effort as upright conduct, purity and interracial fellowship. Read those paragraphs together: the martial language describes moral transformation, and the selected paragraph includes the believers’ own instincts among the obstacles. The initial supplied omission remains. How does beginning with one’s own conduct alter a response to external opposition?
shortened: ...the valiant warriors struggling in the name and for the Cause of Baha'u'llah must, of necessity, encounter stiff resistance, and suffer many a setback. Their own instincts, no less than the fury of conservative forces, the opposition of vested interests, and the objections of a corrupt and pleasure-seeking generation, must be reckoned with, resolutely resisted, and completely overcome. As their defensive measures for the impending struggle are organized and extended, storms of abuse and ridicule, and campaigns of condemnation and misrepresentation, may be unloosed against them.

order.why: The opening of The Advent of Divine Justice describes the effects of contemporary upheaval on communities and institutions in 1938. The following example concerns restrictions in continental Europe. Read the questions within that historical letter, rather than treating its present tense as a report about today. How does the surrounding social setting help explain the pressures on a religious community?

The message of 25 June 1953 in Citadel of Faith addresses a particular period of expansion. The supplied extract omits the beginning and end of a long sentence; the ending directs each person to act according to strength and resources. Consult the complete sentence at the linked source. How does this qualification shape the relation between resolve and capacity?

The World Order of Bahá’u’lláh discusses the future development of institutions as well as spiritual life. The supplied ellipsis crosses a quotation of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá; small transcription differences also remain. Read the full discussion without turning its future assurance into a dated forecast. What kinds of preparation are consistent with the moral responsibilities described earlier in the guide?
shortened: Peoples, nations, adherents of divers faiths, will jointly and successively arise to shatter its unity, to sap its force, and to degrade its holy name. They will assail not only the spirit which it inculcates, but the administration which is the channel, the instrument, the embodiment of that spirit. For as the authority with which Baha'u'llah has invested the future Baha'i Commonwealth becomes more and more apparent, the fiercer shall be the challenge which from every quarter will be thrown at the verities it enshrines.

order.why: The Universal House of Justice’s letter of 26 November 1974 sent a compilation on opposition to National Spiritual Assemblies. Its preceding paragraph leaves the manner of sharing the material to consultation and local judgment. Read the whole letter, including that practical discretion, and preserve its institutional authorship. How might the needs of different communities affect the way such material is studied?

This is the concluding assurance of God Passes By, written after its account of the first century of the Faith. The preceding paragraph describes work still unfinished at that historical moment. Read its hope with those responsibilities and with the guide’s passages on prudence, justice and service. What would responsible confidence look like in the face of uncertainty?

questions: How do the readings distinguish lack of knowledge, disagreement, rejection, slander and persecution? Compare the accounts of recognition with the investigations and disputed reports. What evidence would a fair judgment require?

What do the complete historical narratives reveal about the people affected by persecution, including children, displaced families and those accused for another person’s act? Which examples of help across religious boundaries stand out, and why?

How do steadfastness, prudence and freedom of choice appear together? Compare permission to leave or hide, restrictions on correspondence, and the instruction not to blame those held back by fear. Which details show that a direction belongs to a particular time and place?

How can goodwill toward an aggressor coexist with truthful testimony, boundaries and protection of the vulnerable? Compare Matthew 5:43–48, the counsels against retaliation, and the petitions for inquiry and public justice. What similarities and differences can the texts support?

How do the sources interpret suffering as a possible occasion for spiritual growth while also asking for relief? Read the prayers as whole units, then compare the warnings against negligence and provocation. What responsibilities remain when a person or community affirms hope?

What work do moral conduct, unity, education and service perform in the response to opposition? Explore the actual neighboring subjects and the historical institutional letters. How might studying a difficult passage change both one’s understanding and one’s treatment of other people?
